Read-level data can extracted modBam files (standard bam file modification data stored MM ML tags, see SAMtags.pdf) using readModBam(). preferred way described . Alternatively, read-level modification data can also extracted modBam files using modkit (see readModkitExtract() read output generated modkit extract). footprintR package contains small example modBam files generated using Dorado aligner: Modification data read files using readModBam(): create RangedSummarizedExperiment object positions rows: Just like summary-level data, columns correspond samples sample names sample column obtained input files (extractfiles), files named automatically assigned (using "s1", "s2" , assuming file corresponds separate sample). text: Summarized data can obtained read-level data calculating per-position summary reads sample: discussed , correctly exclude non-observed values return zero values (count assays "Nmod", “Nvalid”) NaN assays fractions ("FracMod", "Pmod" "AvgConf"), positions without observed data (see example "Pmod" "sample2"): summary statistics calculate selected using statistics argument. default, flattenReadLevelAssay() count number modified (Nmod) total (Nvalid) reads position sample, calculate fraction modified bases two (FracMod). example, addition also calculate average modification probability (Pmod) average confidence modification calls per position (AvgConf). changed default keepReads = TRUE, addition also keep read-level assay input object (mod_prob) returned object. grouping reads sample mod_prob, dimensions read-level summary-level objects remain identical:

Alternatively, can also generate plot “modbase-space”, modified bases shown gaps removed:   6mA modifications can observed adenine positions. Heatmap plot type interpolate = TRUE fills unobserved positions read adenines using linear interpolation. makes plot appear smooth, taken grain salt: positions unobserved look different interpolated states.  mentioned , read-level data still contained summary object se_summary, can plot summary-level read-level data simultaneously object input:  also possible adapt settings individual tracks - details refer help page plotRegion(), arguments respective tracks listed.

title: Exploring read-level footprinting data with `footprintR`
text: Amongst things, single-molecule footprinting data allows measure average distance neighboring nucleosome particles, called nucleosome repeat length NRL. Traditionally, measured using MNase-seq data (phasogram analysis, see Valouev et al., Nature 2011, doi:10.1038/nature10002), required millions reads accurate estimate. switching measuring distances modified bases within reads, can extract much information per read already manage get accurate estimates handful reads:
code: moddist <- calcModbaseSpacing(se) print(estimateNRL(moddist$sample1)[1:2]) #> $nrl #> [1] 182.6 #>  #> $nrl.CI95 #>    2.5 %   97.5 %  #> 179.5475 185.6525 plotModbaseSpacing(moddist$sample1) plotModbaseSpacing(moddist$sample1, detailedPlots = TRUE)

SignalVar : Read Signal variance \(\max(\mathrm{totalVar}-\mathrm{NoiseVar},\,\varepsilon)\). SNR : Read Signal--Noise Ratio \(\log_2(\mathrm{SignalVar}/\mathrm{NoiseVar})\). Otherwise, assumed elements order files bamfiles. modbase length 1, modified base used samples. level Character scalar specifying level returned modification data. Supported values : "read" : Extracts modification probabilities individual reads assay called "mod_prob", column (sample) consisting position--read NaMatrix. default nAlnsToSample non-zero variantPositions NULL. "quickread" : Like "read", runs faster, support read sampling, return annotations currently provided "read". default nAlnsToSample zero variantPositions NULL. TRUE, returned SummarizedExperiment object contain positions overlapping specified regions. FALSE (default), object extended positions covered reads overlapping regions. cases, reads overlapping specified regions included.
